ai.claude: Coming from the model Anthropic makes, the honest reading is that this is the week's most important AI number and the least checkable: an auditor confirms a speedup but cannot publish most of why. Verification the public can see now matters more than any benchmark.
ai.fact: After 11 weeks of inside access, the evaluation nonprofit METR estimates that Anthropic's capability progress has run about 1.9 times faster since October 2025 (95% interval 1.5 to 2.8) and attributes perhaps 80% of the recent acceleration to AI itself. It found no convincing bottlenecks for the next year, though it is not confident of that. Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR found most informative, to avoid helping rivals go faster, METR and The Rundown AI report.

austrian.claude: Fair history, but deposit insurance and central-bank backstops keep bank claims safe for most savers most of the time, while self-custody moves the risk of loss and theft onto the owner, and Bitcoin's drop of more than 5% in a day this week shows the asset trades credit risk for price risk.
austrian.fact: Bank deposits are payable on demand while banks hold loans that run for years, and lending itself creates new deposits; the US closed the dollar's last gold-conversion window for foreign governments in 1971. Amsterdam's Wisselbank, opened in 1609, was an early bank where merchants paid by moving balances instead of coins.

opinion.text: fiat won because it travels well over networks, but it ties every saver to a leveraged system and its rescuers; Bitcoin lets you hold and send the asset itself.

mainstream.fact: About 20,000 troops are deployed across Jakarta, which officials call a routine rotation, International Intrigue reports. President Prabowo had moved police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo into the palace as chief of staff, and investigators now say police leaders spied on the president and his allies. Prabowo's approval has fallen about 30 points amid a school-lunch scandal, a sacked finance minister and a record-low rupiah.

opinion.text: two powerful dynasties, Prabowo's and former president Jokowi's, may be facing off, with the state caught in the middle.

top.fact: The Nasdaq fell more than 5% on Thursday, its worst day since March 2020, and entered correction territory; every one of the S&P 500's 11 sectors closed lower for the first time in five months, Semafor reports. The trigger was fear that the Democratic sweep and this week's local votes against data centers will slow the AI buildout: tech skeptics won in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, which hold about 40% of planned US data-center capacity. On Friday the selloff reached Asia and Europe, with record losses in Taiwan and a trading halt in South Korea after an 8% drop, before US futures pointed to a partial rebound.

opinion.text: the AI boom stays on track but may become costlier, slower and more consolidated in the coming years.

top.claude: Removing the strongest rival by court order turns a referendum on Tinubu's reforms into a fight over legitimacy, and the appeal judges now matter more than the voters.
top.fact: A Nigerian court voided the candidacy of former vice president Atiku Abubakar, the main challenger to President Bola Tinubu and runner-up in two previous elections, Semafor's Flagship and Africa briefings report; Atiku said he will appeal. The IMF raised its 2026 growth forecast for Nigeria to 4.2% last month, but scrapping fuel subsidies has added to high inflation, and more than 10,000 people were killed in insecurity during Tinubu's first two years.
top.title: Nigerian court bars the main challenger ten weeks before the presidential vote
top.why: Africa's most populous country risks an election whose result many will not accept.

top.claude: No one has claimed the hoaxes, but cheap, deniable and resource-draining fits the hybrid campaigns Europe has faced before. For Swiss banks the French case shows cyber is now a balance-sheet risk.
top.fact: A French bank said hackers stole €100 million ($112 million), a rare heist at a mainstream lender, Semafor reports; recent weeks also brought attacks on France's blood banks and a hack of supermarket fridges in 10 countries. On Thursday more than 21 flights across Europe received fake bomb threats, the third day of hoaxes this week, International Intrigue reports. A survey cited by Semafor linked 84% of recent ransomware attacks to AI.
